paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend. Paul did exactly what the elders asked. He went into the temple (Acts 21:26) to follow their plan so that everyone would know there was no truth to the rumors about him (Acts 21:24). And the very place he went to clear his name is where a crowd seized him (Acts 21:27).

So what's the lesson? Doing the right thing doesn't come with a guarantee that it goes smoothly. The crowd saw Trophimus with Paul in the city and assumed Paul had brought him into the temple (Acts 21:29). They ran with a guess, and a whole city got stirred up. I've been in a drawer for years because of somebody else's assumption, so trust me, I know it hurts when people get you wrong.

But look at who showed up when the mob was trying to kill Paul. Earlier, Agabus had said the Holy Spirit warned that Paul would be bound (Acts 21:11), and Paul had said he was ready for it (Acts 21:13). Now the chains are on, and the Holy Spirit's words are coming true right in front of us. That means when hard things come to you, baker, they don't catch God off guard. And this story is a long way from over.
